1.1: The Hebrew describes residing as a stranger in the “fields of Moab”; BSB uses “reside in the land of Moab.”
1.2: The Hebrew repeats “name” for the man, his wife, and his two sons, with singular “name” for the two sons together. It calls Moab’s territory “fields,” rendered “land” in BSB.
1.4: The Hebrew says they lived “there”; BSB explicitly supplies “in Moab.”
1.5: The Hebrew calls her “the woman”; BSB identifies her as Naomi.
1.6: The Hebrew first says that she rose and returned, then explains what she had heard. BSB puts her hearing first and describes her as preparing to leave; it renders “bread” as “food.”
1.8: The Hebrew refers simply to “the dead”; BSB adds the possessive “your.”
1.9: The Hebrew says they “lifted their voice and wept”; BSB combines these actions into “wept aloud.” It adds “new” to the husband.
1.11: The Hebrew commands “return” without an explicit “home”; BSB supplies “home.”
1.12: The Hebrew has no separate adjective for “another” husband or explicit destination “home.” It introduces the possibility with “if I said,” rendered “if I thought” in BSB.
1.13: The Hebrew describes her condition as “very bitter”; BSB renders this as “it grieves me very much.” It repeats “for them” in both questions, which BSB states only in the first.
1.14: The Hebrew says they “lifted their voice and wept” again; BSB has “wept aloud.” The kiss has no separate word corresponding to “goodbye.”
1.15: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and repeats “your sister-in-law” in the return command. BSB supplies Naomi and replaces the second sister-in-law with “her.”
1.16: The Hebrew uses the verb for spending the night; BSB renders it as “live.” The statements “your people, my people” and “your God, my God” contain no explicit future verb.
1.17: The Hebrew’s oath literally says “thus may the LORD do to me, and thus may He add”; BSB makes the punishment and its severity explicit. BSB also supplies “anything but” before death.
1.18: The Hebrew leaves both women unnamed and says she stopped speaking to her. BSB supplies Naomi and Ruth and specifies that she stopped “trying to persuade her.”
1.19: The Hebrew says “the two of them,” where BSB supplies Naomi and Ruth. The speakers are marked by a feminine plural verb; BSB explicitly identifies them as “the women of the city.”
1.22: The Hebrew describes the territory of Moab as “fields”; BSB uses “land.”

2.2: The Hebrew has singular “the field”; BSB uses plural “the fields.” The answer leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Naomi.
2.3: The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and repeats the root of happening in “her chance happened”; BSB names Ruth and expresses the chance with “happened to come.”
2.5: The Hebrew calls the foreman “his young man who was stationed over the reapers”; BSB compresses this into “the foreman of his harvesters.”
2.6: The Hebrew explicitly calls her a “Moabite young woman” and describes the territory as Moab’s “field.” BSB has “the Moabitess” and “the land of Moab.”
2.7: The Hebrew says she “stood” or remained from morning until now; BSB uses “has continued.” The place of her brief sitting is called “the house,” rendered “the shelter” in BSB.
2.8: The Hebrew begins with the question “Have you not heard, my daughter?” BSB changes this to the command “Listen, my daughter.”
2.9: The Hebrew asks “Have I not commanded the young men ...?” BSB turns this into “Indeed, I have ordered the young men.” It describes the water as what the young men draw, where BSB describes filled jars.
2.11: The Hebrew uses the explicit time expression “yesterday, the day before yesterday”; BSB renders it as “before.”
2.12: The Hebrew wishes that her reward may be “complete”; BSB renders it as “rich” and makes receiving the reward explicit.
2.13: The Hebrew says he spoke “to the heart of your maidservant”; BSB renders this bodily expression as “spoken kindly to your maidservant.” It has no separate word for “continue.”
2.14: The Hebrew calls the liquid “vinegar”; BSB expands this to “vinegar sauce.” It explicitly mentions “your morsel,” where BSB uses “it” for the bread.
2.15: The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed, where BSB supplies her name. The permission to glean among the sheaves is stated directly; BSB frames it as “Even if she gathers.”
2.16: The Hebrew emphatically repeats the root of pulling out; BSB uses a single “pull out.”
2.17: The Hebrew leaves the woman unnamed; BSB supplies Ruth.
2.18: The Hebrew says she gave her what she had left from being satisfied. BSB explicitly supplies “her meal” and identifies the recipient as Naomi.
2.19: The Hebrew says she told her mother-in-law about the person with whom she had worked; BSB says she told her “where she had worked.”
2.20: The Hebrew explicitly says that the man is “near to us”; BSB calls him “a close relative.”
2.22: The Hebrew says to “go out” with his young women; BSB uses “work with.” It describes unnamed people encountering or harming her in another field, where BSB has impersonal “nothing will happen to you.”
2.23: The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and separately names the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; BSB names Ruth and combines the two harvests.

3.1: The Hebrew leaves Ruth unnamed and has no separate “One day.” BSB supplies both her name and that introductory time expression.
3.2: The Hebrew says she “was with” his young women; BSB explicitly says she had been working with them.
3.3: The Hebrew says to anoint herself and put on her clothes; BSB specifies “perfume” and “best clothes.”
3.5: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB identifies her as Ruth.
3.7: The Hebrew says Boaz’s “heart was glad”; BSB renders this as being “in good spirits.” It leaves the woman unnamed and calls the heap simply “the heap,” where BSB supplies Ruth and “of grain.”
3.8: The Hebrew calls the startled person “the man”; BSB supplies Boaz.
3.9: The Hebrew repeats “your maidservant,” where BSB uses “your servant” and then “me.” The word for spreading his “wing” is rendered “the corner of your garment” in BSB.
3.10: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Boaz. It lists “poor” before “rich,” reversing BSB’s order, and speaks of going after the young men rather than running after them.
3.11: The Hebrew says “all the gate of my people” knows; BSB renders this communal image as “all my fellow townspeople.”
3.13: The Hebrew first says “if he will redeem you”; BSB explicitly makes this “if he wants to redeem you.” In the second condition the Hebrew itself explicitly names willingness.
3.14: The Hebrew says she rose before a man could recognize his companion; BSB changes this to anyone else recognizing her. The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies Boaz.
3.15: The Hebrew says he measured six of barley and placed it on her; BSB says he “shoveled six measures” into the shawl. The unit and the second reference to the shawl are supplied in BSB.
3.16: The Hebrew literally asks “Who are you, my daughter?”; BSB renders the question as “How did it go, my daughter?” It supplies the names Ruth, Naomi, and Boaz where the Hebrew leaves the women unnamed and calls him “the man.”
3.18: The Hebrew’s command is “sit”; BSB uses “Wait” and supplies Naomi as speaker. The matter literally “falls,” rendered “things go” in BSB.

4.1: The Hebrew explicitly says Boaz “went up” to the gate and refers to the other man with an unnamed-person formula. BSB omits the upward direction and addresses him as “my friend.”
4.2: The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies Boaz. It explicitly repeats that they sat, where BSB uses “did so.”
4.3: The Hebrew says Naomi “has sold” the portion of the field; BSB has “is selling.” Moab’s territory is called “fields,” rendered “land” in BSB.
4.4: The Hebrew uses the image “uncover your ear,” rendered “inform you” in BSB. The negative condition has third-person “he will not redeem,” whereas BSB addresses the man as “you will not redeem.”
4.5: The Hebrew describes buying the field “from the hand of Naomi”; BSB renders this as buying it “from Naomi.”
4.6: The Hebrew repeats the redemption root in the command “redeem for yourself my redemption”; BSB renders this as “Take my right of redemption.”
4.7: The Hebrew joins redemption and exchange with “and”; BSB uses “or” and explicitly supplies “of property.” It calls the recipient the man’s “companion,” where BSB has “the other party.”
4.8: The Hebrew places the speech before removing the sandal; BSB puts removing the sandal first.
4.9: The Hebrew says “I have acquired,” where BSB has “I am buying.” It repeats “all that belonged to” for the property of Chilion and Mahlon and uses the image “from Naomi’s hand.”
4.10: The Hebrew repeats “the name of the deceased,” where BSB uses “his name” on the second occurrence. It describes the name as not being “cut off,” rendered “disappear” in BSB.
4.11: The Hebrew’s final commands literally say to “do valor” and “call a name”; BSB renders them as wishes to be prosperous and famous.
4.13: The Hebrew says Boaz “went in to her” and that the LORD “gave her conception”; BSB uses “had relations with her” and “enabled her to conceive.”
4.14: The Hebrew wishes that his name “may be called in Israel”; BSB makes the renown explicit with “become famous.”
4.15: The Hebrew describes him as “a restorer of soul” and sustaining her “gray hair”; BSB uses the verbs “renew your life” and “sustain you in your old age.”
4.17: The Hebrew first says the neighboring women called a name for him, then repeats that they called his name Obed. BSB combines this into a single naming statement.
4.18: The Hebrew actively says Perez “begot” Hezron; BSB expresses this as Perez “was the father of” Hezron.
4.19: The Hebrew actively uses “begot” for both generations; BSB uses “was the father of.”
4.20: The Hebrew actively uses “begot” for both generations; BSB uses “was the father of.”
4.21: The Hebrew actively uses “begot” for both generations; BSB uses “was the father of.”
4.22: The Hebrew actively uses “begot” for both generations; BSB uses “was the father of.”
